question: Can cheap unordered source statistics safely own a prospective publishability gate for speculative r25 search?

environment.zstd_cli: *** Zstandard CLI (64-bit) v1.5.7, by Yann Collet ***

shuffled.construction: deterministic permutation of the exact same byte multiset

shared_facts: identical exact multiset of 512 fixed-size 64 KiB chunks
therefore identical byte histogram and identical unordered chunk hashes

decision: NARROW_CHEAP_PREFILTER_FAMILY. File count/size, byte histogram or entropy, and unordered chunk/content-feature bags cannot safely bound attainable compressed bytes: exact shared facts can coexist with orders-of-magnitude different outcomes. Issue #194 should reject empirical thresholds on those facts. Reopen prospective pruning only with order-aware, grammar-aware forced state that is mathematically unavoidable under every continuation, or move to exact execution sharing that avoids recomputing losing speculative work.
mandatory_hostile_preserved: ML remains the product hostile: a +116 B pre-overlay gap can become a 161,843 B winner, so any safe bound must fail open there.
next_discriminator: Execute the already-frozen grouped historical-dict integrated A/B on Shifted, Boundary, False Neighbors and Incompressible for v0.28 plus the current discovery-neutral attempt-5 child. Preserve exact candidate/final archive identity, candidate/assignment/locality facts, and measure child wall/CPU/process-tree RSS/temp-I/O plus complete-product create wall.
